json.title: Alert Navigator 500: SQL references non-existent column `anh.end_to_end_id`
json.body:
## Summary

`GET /api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/:alertId` returns HTTP 500. The Alert Navigator tab fails to load for every alert.

Reproduced on beta with alert `1025`, tenant `TAZAMA`:

```
API request failed: /api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/1025?tenantId=TAZAMA
Failed to run SQL query on Gold Lakehouse: Request failed with status code 500
```

## Root cause

The Spark SQL sent to the Gold Lakehouse `/execute_sql` endpoint references `anh.end_to_end_id`, but the deployed `alert_navigator_header` view does not expose that column.

Upstream error from `biar-datalakehouse-api` on tazama-c:

```
pyspark.errors.exceptions.captured.AnalysisException:
[UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION] A column or function parameter with name
`anh`.`end_to_end_id` cannot be resolved.
Did you mean one of the following?
[`anh`.`tenant_id`, `anh`.`tx_msg_id`, `anh`.`alert_id`, `anh`.`case_id`, `anh`.`evaluation_id`]
```

Columns actually exposed by the view (from the Spark logical plan):
`tx_msg_id, alert_id, tenant_id, case_id, tx_type, alert_timestamp, alert_reason, alert_type, prediction_outcome, priority, priority_score, evaluation_id, alert_status, ingested_at_ts, pk, transaction_status, transaction_id, transaction_amount, transaction_currency, block_or_override_status, alert_date`.

The bad references live in `backend/src/modules/gold-lakehouse/alerts-lakehouse.service.ts` — in the `SELECT` list (~line 87) and the `GROUP BY` (~line 140).

## Why it broke

The column was a copy-paste leftover from the pre-refactor query, which read directly from the `transactions` table (where `end_to_end_id` does exist). When the query was rewritten to use the `alert_navigator_header` view (commit `992bd5a2`, 2026-04-03), the column reference was preserved in the SQL but the response mapping (`alertMetadata`) was rewritten and no longer reads it. So the field became dead-in-response and invalid-against-schema simultaneously. The bug is latent on `origin/dev` and `paysys/*` branches.

The BIAR view has never exposed `end_to_end_id` in its current shape (verified against the deployed schema and the ETL that writes it). This is a CMS-only fix — no lakehouse change required.

## Verified unused

Full audit of the alert-navigator response path:

- `alertMetadata` mapping (`alerts-lakehouse.service.ts:154-165`) reads only: `alert_id`, `transaction_id`, `alert_timestamp`, `tx_type`, `transaction_amount`, `transaction_currency`, `alert_status`, `alert_reason`, `block_or_override_status`, `evaluation_id`. **`end_to_end_id` is never read.**
- Response type `AlertNavigatorDataResponse` has no `endToEndId` field.
- Frontend (`frontend/src/features/cases/components/view/visualizations/alertnavigator/`) has zero references to `endToEnd` / `end_to_end` in the tab, its service, its types, or its tests.

Other backend hits for `end_to_end_id` are in unrelated endpoints (transaction-detail, transaction-history, condition-lakehouse) that read from `transactions` / `transaction_detail` / `transaction_history` — those tables do have the column and those endpoints are fine. Do not touch them.

## Impact

Alert Navigator tab is completely unusable in beta. No degraded mode — the request 500s and the UI shows nothing.

## Fix

Delete the two `anh.end_to_end_id` lines from the SQL in `alerts-lakehouse.service.ts`:

- Line ~87 (`SELECT` list)
- Line ~140 (`GROUP BY`)

No response-shape change, no frontend impact, no type changes needed. If `RawAlertNavigatorHeaderRow` (or equivalent) has an `end_to_end_id` field, drop that too — but grep before assuming it exists.

## Verification steps

- After patch, hit `GET /api/v1/lakehouse/alert-navigator/1025?tenantId=TAZAMA` and confirm 200.
- Confirm Alert Navigator tab renders on an existing case in beta.
- Existing unit tests should pass unchanged (they don't assert on `endToEndId`).

## Follow-up (separate)

`GoldLakehouseService.runSqlQuery` swallows the upstream response body — only `Request failed with status code 500` surfaces in CMS logs, forcing an SSH into the lakehouse host to diagnose. Worth logging `error.response?.data` on axios failures so the actual Spark error appears in CMS backend logs. File separately if we agree.
